A small hardware store stands in the shadow of a corporate chain in your local downtown area. Despite its size, this local gem thrives, not in spite of its modest scale, but because of it. Here, the owner isn't just a shopkeeper. They're a trusted neighbor who knows not only your home improvement needs but also your family's projects, challenges, and triumphs. . He knows the town, too. He knows the local traditions, holidays, stresses and joys. He knows when the weather is about to turn icy or what time of day traffic is likely to be a nightmare. He knows how to use this knowledge for tailored local marketing efforts.

It’s with this intimate knowledge the hardware store crafts tailored promotions, hosts community events, and fosters a sense of belonging that no corporate giant can match. And it all happens locally, in your neighborhood.

[According to our research](https://www.salesforce.com/products/resources/state-of-the-connected-customer/), 80% of shoppers say that the experience a company provides is just as important as its products or service. As a marketer, if you know where your customers live and what they need, you're that much closer to being able to connect on a deeper level. The better you know your audience, the more specifically you can tailor to their needs using [marketing software](https://www.salesforce.com/marketing/).

As we dive into the world of local marketing, we’ll look at specific cases, tactics, and options for how this intimacy fuels success within the heart of communities.

## What is local marketing?

Local marketing refers to the strategies and tactics businesses can use to promote their products or services to potential customers within a specific geographic area. If you’re a small business (SMB) operating in a small region, local marketing is an invaluable tool for reaching and connecting with your target audience.

Unlike large corporations with nationwide or global reach, small businesses often rely heavily on their immediate community for customers and support. Local marketing enables you to focus your efforts on the areas where your target customers are most likely to be found. By understanding the demographics, preferences, and behaviors of the local community, you can tailor your marketing messages and promotions.

Compared to traditional mass marketing efforts, local marketing can offer significantly higher returns on investment for small businesses. Imagine a small bakery invests $1,000 in a broad online advertising campaign targeting a wide audience across the entire city. This campaign reaches 10,000 people, but only 100 of them convert into customers, resulting in a conversion rate of 1%.

Now, consider a local marketing push by the same bakery. Instead of casting a wide net, they invest the same $1,000 in targeted Facebook ads specifically aimed at residents within a 5-mile radius of their storefront. This localized campaign reaches only 2,500 people, a quarter of the audience of the broad campaign. However, due to the relevance of the ads and their proximity to the bakery, 200 people convert into customers, doubling the conversion rate to 8%.

While the broad advertising campaign reached a larger audience, the local marketing approach achieved significantly higher conversion rates.
